classification: SCOPED SHAPE-DISSIPATION CONDITIONAL REGULARITY / SLICEWISE RANK-ONE OR AFFINE COMPACTNESS / NO AUTOMATIC GOOD SCALE / OPEN / NOT CLAY
completed_claims: For every finite M, a local suitable weak pair near closure Q1 with A(1)+E(1)+D(1)<=M and Theta(grad u) in L2_t H1_x is regular at the terminal centre if integral_Q1 |grad Theta|^2<epsilon_Theta(M), where Theta(G)=d(G)G/|G|^(3/2), zero at G=0, and d is distance to all rank<=1 matrices.

For smooth-preterminal compatible gradients, Theta crosses the full zero set through (F-delta)_+ B and integral |grad Theta|^2<=(2+1/sqrt2)^2 integral Gamma. Hence sufficiently small full-gradient shape dissipation Gamma=|G| |grad(G/|G|)|^2 under the same M cap implies local regularity. This classical Gamma expression is not assigned automatically to arbitrary suitable weak solutions.

Small Theta derivatives give spatially constant slice limits after Poincare and legitimate time-dependent Fatou subsequences. Zero constant uses weak second-minor closure to give rank<=1 gradients; nonzero constant uses continuous inversion and a gradient-L2 contradiction to give affine velocity slices. A nonzero affine NS example excludes a rank-one-only conclusion.

The slice union gives tr(G^2)=beta(t), with beta measurable and bounded by the uniform slice velocity energy. Subtract p0=-beta|x|^2/6 and integrate only the harmonic pressure gradient. The corrected solenoidal equation has an L2 force including bounded -grad p0, so the already justified RS small-power bootstrap yields C_limit(r)<=K_u*r^(1/7).

Strong near-pressure convergence, harmonic q_n and pi-p0, and the quadratic p0 remainder O(r^6) permit fixed-r then n-to-infinity transfer to the original suitable solutions and a fixed unforced CKN threshold.

The normalized Theta-gradient and Gamma integrals scale as r^(-1) times their physical integrals. Singular-centre lower bounds only apply at scales satisfying the same M cap. Nested bounds are not independent costs; even valid disjoint-shell lower bounds of order r remain summable. No contradiction with finite total shape dissipation is obtained.
open_items: Same-solution NS evolution producing an arbitrarily small prescribed-centre scale with both a common A+E+D cap and normalized Theta-gradient or Gamma below its threshold remains unproved.
Finite GD/SG/LK integrals and weak measure terminal traces do not establish cross-scale contraction, a non-summable disjoint concentration cost, or concentration exclusion.
No automatic full weak-H1 admissibility or classical Gamma definition for every suitable weak solution is claimed; the general SC-A theorem expressly requires Theta's full weak spatial derivative.
No effective epsilon(M), regularity-radius modulus, optimality, complete novelty audit, or human peer review is provided.
General unforced three-dimensional global regularity, a singularity construction, and the Clay goal remain open.

Start from the exact local full-gradient Frobenius entropy balance, retain transport, cutoff, initial/final slice and pressure-Hessian terms, and compute each term's NS scaling. Check whether any cross-scale decay or non-summable disjoint concentration cost can be derived while controlling A+E+D by a common M. Read GD and the relevant earlier local entropy/pressure-gate sources before using them; do not redo unchanged global radial or variable-axis tests as new research. Keep any uncontrolled critical term explicit. Do not repeat SC compactness or promote finite total dissipation, a weak terminal measure trace, another conditional reformulation or finite experiments to an arbitrary-evolution proof. Effective thresholds and source-collision audits are separate questions. No publication or reverse-runtime inspection.
